simon raymonde.note: bassist of Cocteau Twins and founder of the influential UK label Bella Union (Fleet Foxes, Beach House); 'Heaven or Los Angeles' riffs on the Cocteau Twins album title for a dream-pop/4AD-adjacent DJ set.

muku.note: Thin public footprint — mostly turns up as Fabiano do Nascimento's regular DJ-set opener/closer (also played alongside him at Chicago's Constellation), so treat this as a wildcard low-key close rather than a known quantity.

dj tennis.note: Manfredi Romano — Italian scene godfather who founded Life and Death in 2010 (Tale Of Us, Mind Against and Carlita all came up through the label); a globally touring, melodic house/techno selector with real ties to the Innervisions crowd via the Rakastella festival.

kaz james.note: Australian DJ/producer with old-school pedigree — a decade-long Pacha Ibiza residency (Nic Fanciulli's 'We Are The Night') behind him, now making straight-up house that's charted with tracks like 'Not in Love' and 'Footprints.'

propersoundco.note: No clear public bio surfaced — reads as this session's co-presenting sound/production crew (the 'Vol. 2' branding) rather than a separate DJ booking; can't verify further.

capes.note: LA underground house DJ/producer (Ray Barragan), half of club tularosa — small-room circuit, emotionally-charged sets over pure peak-time function.

sinéad.note: Reads as a San Francisco-based selector — groove-forward, house-heavy, hypnotic sets. Couldn't confirm this is the same Sinéad playing LA regularly, so treat as unverified.

floorplan.note: Robert Hood & daughter Lyric Hood — Detroit techno royalty (M-Plant) turned deep, gospel-inflected house. 'Baby Baby' fills a floor for a reason.

honeyluv.note: Cleveland-born, ex-Navy — one of the biggest tech-house breakouts of the last few years; soulful, groovy end of the genre, runs her own 4 Tha Luv label.

coco and breezy.note: Twin sisters (also the eyewear-brand founders) turned house/dance DJ duo — danceable, R&B-tinged, more crossover-pop energy than underground.

strawbry.note: LA underground fixture (South Florida-raised) — breaks-and-house sets, runs the STUDIO5400 party series.

vieze asbak.note: Dutch 'memecore'/troll-rave artist out of Amsterdam's Pestcore Collectief — hard-dance-adjacent chaos, not clean house or techno. A sign this bill gets weird in spots.

jazzy irl.note: Couldn't pin down a confident bio for this one — flagging as unverified rather than guessing.

kim anh.note: LA queer-underground institution, two decades deep — classic house, garage, minimal-wave leaning; founded the beloved Booby Trap! party and Can U Not Talk Records.

physical therapy.note: Daniel Fisher — Queens-via-Berlin producer known for genre-hopping, slightly off-kilter techno (bongo-flecked, breakbeat-inflected); runs Allergy Season and holds a residency at Nowadays. Real cult following, not a big-room name.

casmalia.note: LA-based bass/tech-house producer on a real hot streak — DoLab stage at Coachella, EDC Vegas, Splash House, direct support for Kyle Watson/Noizu/Diplo, and a track that hit #1 trending on SoundCloud US in late 2025. Festival-friendly, bass-heavy energy rather than deep/vinyl selecting.

emmber.note: LA-based house/techno producer and engineer; thin public footprint beyond production credits, so treat as a supporting local booking rather than a draw.

dj holographic.note: Detroit DJ/producer (Ariel Corley) blending house, disco, Motown, and techno — 2025 debut album 'House In The Dark' leans into Afrofuturism; praised by Carl Craig and The Blessed Madonna, has played Panorama Bar and Smart Bar.

colored craig.note: LA DJ known for soul/funk/jack-leaning house sets — a regular guest at A Club Called Rhonda over the years.

gay felony.note: LA DJ/producer (Melody Scallion) — extended vinyl sets ranging from soulful/progressive house to hard house and melodic techno; hosts a Dublab radio show.

anastazja.note: LA-based DJ (USC grad) who came up through Soulection Radio, played Boiler Room, and recently supported Keinemusik's Rampa — a credential that tracks with the melodic/Keinemusik lane.

axel boman.note: Swedish producer and Studio Barnhus co-founder — playful, eclectic deep house with a loose, jammy feel (his 'Purple Drank' and marathon festival sets are genre-defining); this is basically his label's home-turf party.

kornél kovács.note: Studio Barnhus co-founder alongside Axel Boman — bright, melodic, disco-tinged house; one of the most purely fun-first DJs in the European house scene.

secondcity.note: UK house producer behind 2014's global hit 'I Wanna Feel' and a Grammy-nominated remixer (Fall Out Boy's 'Centuries') — polished, vocal-driven house that's toured festival mainstages for a decade; he and Noizu have a track together ('More Love'), so this pairing tracks.

matthew dear.note: Ghostly International's flagship artist since the early 2000s (also records minimal techno as Audion) — moody, baritone-vocal art-pop laid over deep, European-club-respected production; a real crossover between listening-room songwriting and functional techno.

the juan maclean.note: John MacLean's long-running DFA Records project (James Murphy's label, home of LCD Soundsystem) — NYC dance-punk-turned-disco, best known for 'Happy House'; DJ sets lean house and post-punk-inflected disco.

mesme.note: LA-based (via the Midwest and Singapore) DJ and Into the Woods resident with a monthly dublab show — vinyl-heavy sets blending house, techno, acid, electro and trip-hop; a 2021 Boiler Room appearance and a 2020 EP on Steel City Dance Discs.

aali rehman.note: San Diego-based DJ/producer working deep house, melodic techno and dark disco — thin public footprint, and unclear how regularly they play LA.

wavves.note: Nathan Williams' surf-punk/lo-fi indie project out of San Diego — bratty, noise-caked guitar pop since 2008's 'Wavvves'; a real touring name with an actual catalog, not a local opener.

waax.note: Brisbane, Australia post-punk/garage band fronted by Marie 'Maz' DeVita — raw, emotive, three albums deep (most recently 2026's 'Angel's Mess').

the paranoyds.note: LA garage-rock/indie-punk four-piece out of the local DIY scene — Bratmobile-meets-Go-Go's energy, Third Man-affiliated, played Coachella and opened for Jack White.

modern color.note: Redondo Beach four-piece that started as metalcore and evolved into 'grungegaze' — alt-rock with shoegaze/hardcore edges, in the Hum/Title Fight/Deftones lineage.

korolova.note: Olga Korolova — Ukrainian melodic-techno/progressive-house producer, ex-ballet dancer turned DJ; runs the Captive Soul label/radio show, plays Tomorrowland mainstage and EDC, DJ Mag top-60 (2024).

spice aku bianca maieli dj sudi mtooray.note: LA DJ crew/event series/label built around their shared South Asian heritage — sets range Baile Funk to Bollywood, reggaeton to amapiano, dabke to dancehall; high-energy global club music, not a house/techno night.

ben annand.note: LA electronic scene fixture since the mid-'90s — longtime resident at Moontribe and founder of the Tropical party series (boats, warehouses, the desert); Balearic/tribal-leaning outdoor-party lane.

derrick carter.note: Chicago house legend since the late-'80s Warehouse/Muzic Box lineage — co-runs Classic Music Company with Luke Solomon; funky, genre-agnostic, unmistakable house selection still headlining at this level.

dj heather.note: Chicago house DJ, co-founder of the pioneering all-female Superjane crew (with DJ Colette, Dayhota, Lady D) — soulful, genre-blurring sets rooted in Gramaphone Records digging.

h foundation.note: San Diego duo (Hipp-E & Halo) — dub-inflected deep/tech-house with a Fabric London residency and a Chemical Brothers remix credit to their name; not a frequent LA booking.

hector moralez.note: Oakland-raised, now LA-based house DJ/producer (Minority Music, The Factory labels) — Chicago/Detroit-rooted, soul-deep selections; a regular in Sneak's LA circle.

j dub.note: Chicago-bred new-school house DJ and frequent DJ Sneak collaborator on the LA circuit (CHI♡LA, Certified Groovers) — funky, percussive, seamless-blend style.

jimi jules.note: Zurich-born, Berlin-based (longtime Watergate resident) house producer now signed to Innervisions — jazzy, soulful, musician's-ear house that broke through via 2014's Defected hit 'Pushing On.'

andy oro.note: LA DJ, host of the Oro Hour on VPN Radio and a Made to Move resident — eclectic underground/house sets pulling from DIY dance music, hip-hop and bloghouse.

knoxdotmp3.note: LA-based DJ/producer (KNOX) working house, ballroom and club sounds — released mix series like 'Club Cowboy' and played the VICE Underground 'Cage' night.

flabbergast la.note: LA techno DJ (Miami-raised, DIY rave background) and founder of VICE Underground — heavy drums, acid-driven, high-energy sets built for a transformative dancefloor, not a chill room.

buck off.note: LA DJ who's played Catch One, Los Globos and Avalon — moves from Chicago-style house by day to tech-house after dark; co-founded the Reverb party brand.

mayer hawthorne.note: Michigan-born, LA-based soul/R&B artist who broke via Stones Throw in the late 2000s — smooth blue-eyed soul with real digger credibility behind it, not just a nostalgia act.

kelly finnigan.note: Frontman of Bay Area deep-soul revivalists Monophonics and a well-regarded voice/producer in the current retro-soul scene.

the intruders.note: Philly soul group behind 'Cowboys to Girls' and 'I'll Always Love My Mama' — 60s/70s Gamble & Huff-era originals, not a tribute act.

blue magic.note: Philly soul group behind 'Sideshow' and 'Three Ring Circus' — genuine early-70s vocal-group pedigree on this bill.

joey quiñones.note: Frontman/producer of Thee Sinseers (Colemine Records) — the artist most credited with defining the modern Chicano lowrider 'souldies' revival out of Southern California.

denis dekay.note: Italian techno producer with releases on the well-regarded hard-techno label 999999999 and on No War Records — hypnotic, driving, festival-capable techno. This is a genuine first-ever US show, not a routine tour stop.

aiden ramos.note: LA DJ (Cal State Dominguez Hills, audio recording) and resident selector for Amore Disco — sets move through Balearic, house, disco and rare Italo with deep melodic touches; has played Berlin and Barcelona.

reedster.note: Amore Disco's other resident at Apotheke, playing alongside Aiden Ramos on the room's all-vinyl system — a reliable groove/disco selector, not a touring name.

bones.note: Co-resident (with Lee Wells) of House Heads, the long-running house night at Sound Nightclub in Hollywood -- LA house DJ/producer who's held that residency for years.

lee wells.note: LA-born house DJ/producer, House Heads co-resident since 2011 with residencies at several of LA's top clubs; played Coachella in 2014. Solidly in the LA house-scene establishment, not an underground unknown.

dj perception.note: London (Camberwell) 2-step/UK garage specialist and MoodSwing label head, drawing on 90s US house, garage and jungle — genuine scene pedigree (RA podcast feature, Fresh Milk dubplates), not a hype booking.

louiv.note: SF-based selector and founder of Texture Summit, a key Bay Area underground party/imprint since 2019 — punchy, groove-forward house and garage.

chris cruse.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2001 and founder of Spotlight, the long-running queer-rooted house/techno/disco party — now Berlin-based, plays Panorama Bar and the festival circuit; a tough, sleazy, soulful sound.

soul purpose la.note: LA underground/festival selector (Splash House, Lightning in a Bottle, EDC) blending disco, 90s house, minimal, techno and hard groove — a dancefloor generalist more than a specialist.

alex ho.note: Pasadena-native LA DJ/producer — genre-bending sets spanning vintage boogie, proto-house and techno, plus a debut LP ('Move Through It') on the Dutch deep-digger label Music From Memory.

j rocc.note: LA turntablist and Beat Junkies co-founder, Stones Throw-adjacent — an eclectic crate-digger whose sets range across funk, soul, hip-hop and boogie. Genuine West Coast DJ royalty.

luxxury.note: LA producer Jason Kaplan's nu-disco/boogie alias — glossy, hook-forward throwback dance grooves, closer to Todd Terje's pastiche than straight house.

park jeong min.note: South Korean character actor (Bleak Night, Keys to the Heart, Deliver Us from Evil, Hellbound) — reliably one of the better performers in Korean genre cinema, not a marquee name most casual watchers will recognize.

terrell brooke.note: Founder of TheyHouse LA, a key figure in LA's queer house-music community — curates deep, Chicago-house-rooted lineups. This Sunday Sessions edition is explicitly billed as a celebration of house music's Black and LGBTQIA+ origins, not just a generic day party.

will worden.note: LA-via-Texas country/folk singer — Rolling Stone likened his voice to an Elvis/Gordon Lightfoot blend; his debut LP leans Countrypolitan, nodding to Lee Hazlewood and Glen Campbell.

same ol smile.note: LA country-boogie six-piece formed out of Mystic Braves and Jesus Sons — described as somewhere between the Flying Burrito Brothers and Captain Beefheart.

dj al lover.note: LA psych DJ/producer applying hip-hop sampling technique to the Thee Oh Sees / Ty Segall / White Fence garage-psych scene — a Desert Daze and Levitation Fest regular.

david moscoe.note: The Dresden's house bandleader — his trio anchors the venue's biweekly no-cover jazz/crooner nights alongside rotating singers.

dinabn.note: LA-based DJ affiliated with Club Cielo's Latin American-underground femme collective — limited verifiable bio beyond that affiliation.

voltage.note: UK DnB DJ/producer (real name Rouen Wilkins), one-third of Kings of the Rollers — decade-plus career, versatile across jump-up, jungle and deeper rollers.

ac13.note: Brighton-via-Bristol DnB producer on the rise — releases on Crucast, DnB Allstars and Tomorrowland Music; runs his own label Alpha Circuit.

archie hamilton.note: London DJ/producer/label owner — an early architect of a rugged, atmospheric minimal-house-and-techno sound; MicroHertz label boss and a Paradise Ibiza regular.

dj jenny lsq.note: Resident selector for Sid the Cat's recurring 'Freak Scene' night — free, all-ages indie/punk/old-school record sets in the venue's classroom-turned-lounge bar.

david harness.note: Bay Area deep-house DJ/producer/remixer (credits with Mary J. Blige, Alicia Keys) — soulful, classic house across Coachella, Glastonbury and beyond.

big cee.note: Chris Legaspi — the longtime resident opening DJ at Marques Wyatt's DEEP, a foundational figure in LA's house community who's shared decks with Frankie Knuckles and Louie Vega.

seeps.note: Bronx-born, LA-based DJ steeped in NYC's '90s golden-era house and disco/boogie — has drawn attention from Louie Vega and DJ Sneak.

kublaii.note: Hillsboro, Oregon-raised, Salt Lake City-based indie singer-songwriter blending folk, rock and electronic textures — 40M+ streams and a debut LP ('temujin') due in 2026.

steve von till.note: Neurosis co-founder/vocalist-guitarist — his solo work trades the band's crushing weight for dark, meditative acoustic folk and drone.

six organs of admittance.note: Ben Chasny's long-running psych-folk/drone project since the late '90s — a New Weird America mainstay, prolific collaborator (Comets on Fire, Rangda, MV & EE).

night beats.note: Seattle-formed psych/garage-rock band on The Reverberation Appreciation Society (Levitation's label) — fuzzed-out, surf-tinged garage with real touring chops.

brad mehldau.note: One of the most acclaimed jazz pianists of his generation — known for reharmonizing rock/pop songbooks (Radiohead, Nick Drake) through a jazz lens.

chris thile.note: Mandolin virtuoso, Punch Brothers/Nickel Creek — genre-crossing bluegrass-to-classical musicianship, former host of public radio's 'Live from Here.'

blake mills.note: In-demand guitarist/producer (Bob Dylan, Alabama Shakes, Perfume Genius) — a go-to for artful, texture-first arrangements.

powder.note: Tokyo DJ/producer Momoko 'Moko' Goto — eclectic, colorful disco/house/pop selector known for a widely-circulated Boiler Room Tokyo set.

dj healthy.note: NY-via-Tokyo selector, founder of the PACIFIC MODE party series — tripped-out house and tech.

daphni.note: Dan Snaith's (Caribou) dancefloor-focused alias, running his own Jiaolong label since 2012 — more raw and club-built than his Caribou records, with a strong Afro/global-rhythm bent.

roni size.note: Bristol jungle/DnB pioneer — Reprazent's 'New Forms' won the 1997 Mercury Prize; Full Cycle/Dope Dragon label boss. A legacy name that rarely turns up on a US warehouse bill.

dieselboy.note: Philadelphia DnB institution since the '90s (Human Imprint label) — first American voted into DJ Mag's Drum & Bass Arena top 10, first DnB artist to chart on Billboard's dance chart. Harder, darker end of the genre.

coffintexts.note: Miami producer (Alexandra Muggli) fusing Peruvian/Caribbean percussion with techno, bass and house — TraTraTrax/Club Romantico circle; off-kilter and sensual rather than straight peak-time.

trax unit.note: LA techno duo (Kyle Galindo & Kian Mahroo), Dublab residents and Gyration Station label founders — 90s-rooted, no-nonsense underground techno.

chris pavlov.note: LA vinyl DJ and Burnin' Chancla co-founder — plays warm, dug-up disco and house cuts channeling NYC dancefloor energy; the name behind this recurring hi-fi series.

ben sterling.note: London house/tech-house producer on Diynamic, Crosstown Rebels and Solid Grooves — disco-and-Chicago-house-rooted, championed by Jamie Jones and Patrick Topping.

dean turnley.note: Melbourne house producer working the Detroit/Chicago lineage — stripped, functional, dancefloor-built; broke out with 'Actin' Tough' hitting #1 on the Beatport chart.

walfredo reyes jr.note: Cuban-American percussionist — member of Santana, then Chicago's drummer/percussionist since 2012; decades on the road with Steve Winwood, Jackson Browne and Gloria Estefan. An arena-level name doing a rare, intimate father-daughter jazz-club set.

lucki.note: Chicago rapper who pioneered a melancholic 'alternative trap'/cloud-rap sound as a teenager (2013's Alternative Trap) — a real underground-to-indie-rap draw with a devoted following, well outside the house/techno lane.

jyoty.note: Indian-Dutch, London-based — Rinse FM resident and Boiler Room regular known for blending baile funk, amapiano, dancehall, jungle and UK garage into one set. Not house/techno, but a legitimately international name for a warehouse booking.

cquestt.note: Courtney Hollinquest — LA native, ex-touring backup dancer turned DJ who founded Baile World in 2020 as an Afro-Latina-led party fusing baile funk, reggaeton, dancehall and Black club music.

mango and ginger.note: Brazil-by-way-of-LA DJ duo built around baile funk and Afro-diasporic rhythms; best known for NYC's 'Favela Fridays' at SOB's, also play regularly on the LA/Baile World circuit.

stephanie rangel.note: Local South Pasadena selector with a standing residency at Sid's Bar; also plays disco sets at Let's Go! Disco & Cocktail Club downtown. Groove/disco-leaning, not a touring name.

yola.note: Youth Orchestra Los Angeles — the LA Phil/Dudamel-founded, El Sistema-inspired youth music program; performing alongside the full Phil here, not a separate act.

maxx steele.note: LA-based minimal-house producer/DJ — low profile, mostly plays local nights like this one; couldn't verify anything beyond that, so treat as an unknown quantity rather than a draw.

felix dickinson.note: UK DJ/producer out of the early-90s free-party scene — deep, chuggy, acid-tinged disco and house; runs Cynic Music, holds residencies at Glastonbury's Block9 and Houghton. A real European-disco-underground name, not a tourist booking.

skeme richards.note: Philadelphia-based DJ/collector with ~30 years digging funk & soul 45s — runs the all-45s party Hot Peas & Butta and is a genuinely respected name in vinyl-collector circles, not a random festival-flyer DJ.

naygod.note: Chicago-born, LA-based DJ/producer whose sets move through deep house, ghettotech, and techno; a regular at Akbar and General Lee's and around the LA underground/queer party circuit.

sepp.note: Minimal/tech-house DJ, producer, and label owner who's played Fabric London and Shelter/The Loft Amsterdam — a legitimate European-club-adjacent credit anchoring an otherwise TBA-location night.

degruvme miz honeyp and bella ferrada.note: The resident trio behind The Hustle's recurring global-disco / sexy-house / funk-soul sets at Gold Diggers — no individual bios turned up, but the free-door, 1st-and-3rd-Saturday residency is well documented.

laurel halo.note: Detroit-born, LA-based composer/producer — her 2012 Hyperdub debut 'Quarantine' was The Wire's Album of the Year; moves between techno, ambient and musique concrète rather than sitting in a DJ-set pocket.

baugruppe90.note: German techno duo (Louis Köhler & Paul Vogler) fusing 90s dnb/house/early-2000s-techno textures into a driving, industrial-leaning sound — releases on Sous Music, Steel City Dance Discs, and their own MONTAGE imprint.

partiboi69.note: Melbourne producer (Fintan Bradley) running his own Mutual Pleasure label — ghetto house, Miami bass, Detroit techno and ghettotech smashed together into loud, wild, high-energy sets; a real touring draw, not a support-slot name.

rebolledo.note: Mexico City producer, Cómeme label mainstay (Matias Aguayo's imprint) and half of Pachanga Boys — the duo behind 'Time,' a genuine Balearic-sunset anthem; his solo sets lean weirder — tribal, psychedelic, hypnotic house.

josh teed.note: Classically-trained violinist turned bass-music producer — live sets layer violin, didgeridoo and analog synth over DJ sets, in the Charlesthefirst/CloZee/Govinda festival-bass lineage.

pilo.note: LA producer/sound designer (aka Cameron Ward) — released on Turbo Recordings, has collaborated with Boys Noize; teaches this techno-production intensive at IO Music Academy.

george kahn.note: LA jazz pianist/composer reviving the 1950s-60s West Coast cool sound (Brubeck, Guaraldi lineage); this vocal-group Jazz & Blues Revue (singers Courtney Lemmon, Gina Saputo, Crystal Starr) is a regular Vibrato booking.

matt forbes.note: Jazz vocalist who took over Marty & Elayne's four-decade Dresden residency with co-host Jesse Goddard — an LA Times 'essential' pick for live jazz in LA.

subshift.note: UK tech-house/bass-house producer (Insomniac Records, Tomorrowland Music) with real festival credits — Tomorrowland, Ushuaïa Ibiza, Ministry of Sound, KOKO Camden. This LA date is early in his first proper US tour.

dj masda.note: Japan-born, Berlin-based co-founder of CABARET Recordings — vinyl digger since the '90s pulling from early techno, futurist electro and playful house; RA Podcast/Dimensions pedigree, has played LA's Pattern Bar before.

mesmé.note: LA DJ/producer (debut EP on Mall Grab's Steel City Dance Discs) — vinyl-heavy blends of moody acid, electro, house and trip-hop; Into the Woods and Dublab resident, Boiler Room 2021.

connor mikami.note: Founder of If You Know You Know, the LA party/label series this event IS — longtime local selector working vintage breaks, electro and club records.

mia mia castillo.note: Miami synth-funk/boogie artist — 'In The Moonlight' is her debut LP on modern-funk label Star Creature Universal Vibrations, produced by Toronto's Gil Masuda; intimate, dancefloor-ready bedroom boogie.

king pari.note: LA funk/psych-soul duo of ex-Minneapolis players (Prince-adjacent pedigree) signed to Stones Throw — lands somewhere between Tame Impala's breeziness and the Minneapolis Sound.

funk freaks.note: Santa Ana-rooted, 13-year-running all-vinyl funk/boogie/disco DJ crew and record shop — this is their regular monthly LA night, not a one-off promoter booking.

blazej malinowski.note: Polish, Berlin-based techno producer — founder of the Inner Tension label, deep and hypnotic productions on Semantica and Silent Season.

kameliia.note: Oslo-based techno DJ (Bulgarian-born) — self-described 'mental techno,' driving and atmospheric, releases on Token and SK_eleven; has played Berghain, Fold and Berlin Atonal.

secus.note: LA techno producer (Matt Salamone) — half of Motionen, co-founder of label Ascetic Limited; jazz/metal-informed, hard and agitated techno.

otha.note: Norwegian producer (Othalie Husøy) making hypnotic, slightly off-kilter club-pop off her 'Club 20' EP — shoegaze and disco textures folded into dance music, more leftfield than rooftop-house.

underground resistance.note: The legendary Detroit techno collective founded by Mike Banks and Jeff Mills — militant, stripped-down techno as political statement; a genuinely mythic name to see billed at a small free Lincoln Heights bar show.

esteban adame.note: LA-born pianist/producer/DJ who came up in the East LA rave scene of the '90s and was personally recruited into Underground Resistance by Mad Mike Banks in 2004 — fuses jazz, techno and Detroit soul, real pedigree not a tribute act.

nomadico.note: DJ Dex — a UR alum who recorded for the label and now runs the LA label Yaxteq (this event's co-promoter) — gritty, funk-fueled, hard-hitting techno and electro.

kosmik.note: Runs The Black Lodge, the LA techno/esoteric-electronics crew and label co-presenting tonight — dub-leaning, ritualistic techno.

fea.note: San Antonio Chicana punk band (members formerly of Girl in a Coma), signed to Joan Jett's Blackheart Records — punk/riot-grrrl energy fused with Latin rhythms; last LP produced by Chicana punk legend Alice Bag.

vladimir dubyshkin.note: Russian techno producer/DJ (grew up in Tambov) known for sample-driven, rave-minded techno with a strong '90s throwback edge — a credible underground import, not a tourist-trail booking.

dancing plague.note: Portland darkwave/EBM solo project (Conor Knowles) on Artoffact Records — dramatic, mechanized post-industrial post-punk.

sacred skin.note: LA-based new wave/synthpop/post-punk duo, also on Artoffact Records, touring behind their new LP 'Born In Fire.'

creux lies.note: Sacramento post-punk/darkwave band with real standing in the current goth revival — self-described 'Californian neo-romantic post-punk,' Cleopatra Records lineage.

discip.note: Argentine tech-house/minimal producer (Neuquén) blending tech house with hip-hop-inflected grooves — backed by Jamie Jones, Marco Carola, Michael Bibi and FISHER, squarely the festival-adjacent tech-house lane.

adam sellouk.note: UK-based melodic tech-house/progressive producer, debuted on Insomniac Records with 'Dance Machine' — championed by Vintage Culture, John Summit, Adam Beyer and Mau P.

gabss.note: Brazilian tech-house/deep-tech producer known for an infectious techno-house-acid blend ('No Control,' 'Devil's Music').

welker.note: US house/tech-house producer whose unreleased IDs get played out by CamelPhat, Solomun, Vintage Culture and Gordo — an under-the-radar name with real industry co-signs.

alex lahey.note: Melbourne singer-songwriter (saxophone-playing power-pop/indie-rock) — hooky, wry guitar records in the Alvvays/Courtney Barnett Australian-indie lineage; a real touring artist, oddly booked into a comedy club's showroom rather than a normal rock room.

hannah lew.note: Bassist/singer of SF post-punk trio Grass Widow and darkwave project Cold Beat, now a few years into a self-titled solo run that critics compare to early New Order and Fad Gadget — underground pedigree, not a casual pop booking.

d dan.note: Berlin-based techno DJ/producer, Mala Junta resident and Berghain-circuit name — raw, hypnotic, low-end-heavy techno with none of the retro-revival stuff; rising fast in the European club scene.

hippie death cult.note: Albuquerque heavy-psych/doom trio on Blues Funeral Recordings — respected in the underground stoner-doom touring circuit.

earth tongue.note: New Zealand psych-doom duo, heavy fuzzed-out riffs with a ritualistic bent — a real name within that scene, not a filler support.

earthless.note: San Diego instrumental power trio (Isaiah Mitchell, Mario Rubalcaba, Mike Eginton) — a genuine legend of the heavy-psych/jam underground since 2001, built on side-long krautrock-and-Hawkwind-indebted improvisation. A real 'big name in a small room' booking for that scene.

liberate elemental forces.note: LA-based Indo-cosmic experimental group built around sitar, tabla, and synth — meditative ragas fused with kosmische/spiritual-jazz textures, a genuinely different but complementary opener.

w i t c h.note: Zambian Zamrock originators (We Intend To Cause Havoc), fuzzed-out psych-funk from the early '70s that Now-Again Records' reissue campaign rescued from obscurity — original frontman Jagari Chanda now fronting a touring lineup. A genuine reissue-culture/crate-digger story, not a nostalgia act.

michael grange.note: SoCal guitarist and LA Music Awards "best guitarist" winner — high-energy instrumental fusion mixing jazz, funk, Latin, and blues; a solid local-scene name rather than a touring headliner.

anotr.note: Amsterdam tech-house duo (Jesse van der Heijden & Oguzhan Guney), founders of the No Art label/collective and behind the global hit "Relax My Eyes" — one of the biggest tech-house exports in Europe right now, squarely mainstream-festival-scale.

the yawpers.note: Denver punk-blues trio known for wild live sets — punk energy filtered through Americana grit, a road-dog band with real cult following.

eddie spaghetti.note: Frontman of long-running punk/rock-'n'-roll band Supersuckers — a genuine cult name in the garage/punk scene, not a random feature credit.

luke strand and friends.note: House jazz jam at The Dresden — no info found beyond the room's own listing; treat as a low-key local no-cover night, not a booked touring act.

reiko takahashi.note: Also performs as Rayko — cut the now-cult 1987 city-pop single 'Sunset Road,' then vanished from music for decades. Only publicly confirmed in early 2026 that she was its singer; now LA-based and performing again. A real appearance from a genuine city-pop ghost story, not a tribute act.

rachel troy.note: LA clown/comedy performer (Lee Strasberg-trained, ex-Groundlings) — her solo clown show Baby won Top of the Fest and Best World Premiere at the 2024 Hollywood Fringe Festival.

george aivaliotis.note: LA clown-theater performer named a Just For Laughs 'New Face' in 2019; his solo shows (Soft Animal, Early Man) have toured Hollywood and Edinburgh Fringe.

barry del sherman.note: Veteran LA character actor — the studio exec who fires Lester Burnham in American Beauty, H.B. Ailman in PTA's There Will Be Blood, plus Independence Day and decades of TV guest spots; a recognizable 'that guy' face for a film-literate crowd.

dj shroomie.note: LA deep-house DJ, co-founder of Low Recordings — the collective behind The Airliner's recurring free house nights, also plays around Bar Franca and The Goldfish.

bl4ze.note: LA multimedia artist/DJ, founder of Toxic Haus — an LGBTQ+ BIPOC collective throwing eclectic, Latin-club-leaning parties across LA and Mexico City since 2018, now also its own label (2026).

nick waterhouse.note: LA-based analog-soul revivalist — horn-driven, tape-warm sound descended from early Motown/Stax; a real touring draw in the vintage-soul-revival lane since his 2012 debut Time's All Gone (Innovative Leisure).

mask appeal.note: LA post-punk/deathrock trio of scene veterans (members have played in Detroit Cobras, Neighborhood Brats, The Starlite Desperation) — self-titled EP out 2025 on Slouch Records.

boney james.note: Longtime smooth-jazz saxophonist — multiple Grammy nods, a reliable radio/adult-contemporary name rather than a deep-cuts pick.

sabrosura boyz.note: LA house/tech-house duo (D. Zeledon & J. Torres), roughly a decade in the making — heavy-percussion, groove-forward sets; cosigned by The Martinez Brothers and HoneyLuv, but not yet an established headline name.

d zeledon.note: One half of Sabrosura Boyz, playing an extra solo set on the same bill.

gunnar.note: No verifiable bio — reads as a local DTLA/Agora Records circuit name, not previously documented.

local jerry.note: No verifiable bio — reads as a local name in the Agora Records/Certified Groovers orbit; unconfirmed.

sg lewis.note: British DJ/producer/songwriter — warm, disco-etched dance-pop (albums 'times', 'AudioLust & HigherLove'); has written and produced with Dua Lipa, Robyn and Nile Rodgers.

hot chip.note: Long-running London electronic band (since 2000, early DFA ties) — dance-rock/electropop ('Over and Over,' 'Ready For The Floor') with a big, festival-tested live show.

austin millz.note: Harlem-raised, NYC-based DJ/producer blending hip-hop with dance/house — DJ'd Beyoncé's 'Homecoming' Coachella sets and played Boiler Room NYC.

nala.note: LA-via-Miami producer/DJ (Stefania Aronin) — acid house and indie-dance with a punky, off-kilter edge; Dirtybird signee and Lights Down Low resident who runs the label Mi Domina.

blond ish.note: Canadian-Swiss duo (Anstascia, Vivie-Ann) — melodic/organic house with an eco-conscious rave ethos; co-founded the No.19 Music label.

poolside.note: LA duo (Filip Nikolic, Jeffrey Paradise) who more or less invented 'daytime disco' — slow-motion, sun-baked grooves ('Harvest Moon,' 'Do You Believe'). About as squarely built for a beach day as it gets.

vandelux.note: Vancouver-born, SF-based producer/vocalist (Evan White) — groove-driven electronic/soul/indie; 'Matter of Time' charted on Billboard Dance.

good neighbours.note: UK indie-pop duo (Oli Fox, Scott Verrill) behind 2024's viral hit 'Home' — tropical-leaning, early-2000s-indie-indebted pop, more festival crossover than club.

momo trosman.note: Buenos Aires-born DJ/producer, DJing professionally since 2011 with European tours behind him — dub- and jazz-informed digging across UK/US house, electro and techno; co-runs the Cure Music label.

cromie.note: Zagreb-born, LA-based producer — Balearic-fringe house: crisp grooves, warm melodies and hazy breaks, released via Amadeus Records and Duality Trax.

mark farina.note: Chicago-born, SF-based house legend behind the long-running 'Mushroom Jazz' series — a jazzy, downtempo-inflected strain of house he's been refining since the mid-90s.

josh wink.note: Philadelphia techno/house legend ('Higher State of Consciousness') and Ovum Recordings co-founder since 1994 — still a headline-level booking three decades in.

dj dazy.note: LA house DJ since 1992 — founded the all-female Sister DJs collective, deep and soulful vinyl-rooted sets, part of the West Coast house lineage this bill leans on.

your unkle magik.note: Vinyl-only house selector, a regular on the Certified Groovers/DTLA open-air circuit.

tom carle.note: LA underground DJ working deep/minimal tech-house and techno — longtime host of a DJ podcast since 2018, regular alongside DJ Sneak and J-Dub on the CHI♡LA circuit.

cocteautwinks.note: LA all-vinyl DJ (Mino Sanchez) — a local cult favorite mixing '90s nostalgia with queer/alternative sensibility; visual artist as much as selector.

sweet gloom.note: LA punk band (Jaake Margo, Chris Clark, Morris Carrillo, Avery Okamura) — this is the record release show for their sophomore album 'No Love Lost' (Sneak Dog Records), old-school crooner melodies and big hooks over fast, lovesick punk.

the death chat.note: Jakob Armstrong's LA garage-punk project, self-titled debut out July 2026 — raw, hooky stuff in the Marked Men/Radioactivity/Cheap Time lineage.

rivussy.note: River Collins — non-binary Afro-Caribbean DJ out of LA/North Long Beach blending techno, ghetto house, vogue and club music.

artbat.note: Ukrainian duo (Artur Kryvenko & Vitalii Limarenko) — melodic techno breakout via Solomun's Diynamic label ('Upperground', 'Atlas'); one of the names most responsible for melodic techno's mainstream crossover.

enrico sangiuliano.note: Italian techno producer, one of Drumcode's biggest-selling artists for a stretch (Adam Beyer's label) — hypnotic, sci-fi-tinged peak-time techno built for big rooms.

bt.note: Brian Transeau — one of American trance's founding names since the late-90s, still touring a big, cinematic, melody-forward sound.

adam auburn.note: LA-based house DJ (East Coast-raised, Traxsource DJ Competition winner) who came up through Insomniac's Exchange LA residency and has shared stages with Hot Since 82, Maceo Plex, Derrick Carter, and Louie Vega — a versatile house selector, not a big-ticket headliner.

jose james.note: NYC-based jazz-soul vocalist signed to Blue Note since 2012 — released a Billie Holiday tribute album, came up through Gilles Peterson's Brownswood scene, often billed as 'jazz for the hip-hop generation.'

bobby west.note: LA jazz pianist/composer, a fixture of the local jazz-club and World Stage circuit — concert-level, straight-ahead jazz chops.

jen cardini.note: Jennifer Cardini — French-born, Berlin-based house/techno DJ, 30 years in, founder of the Correspondant label (grew out of her Rex Club Paris residency, now Kompakt-distributed) spanning deep house, Italo, cosmic disco and techno.

konduku.note: Ruben Üvez — Dutch producer based in Berlin, releases on Nous'klaer Audio and Delsin — hypnotic, detail-heavy techno with a UK bass-culture streak; a selector's selector, not a big-room name.

buttechno.note: Pavel Milyakov — Moscow underground fixture (John's Kingdom collective, tight with Gost Zvuk and Klasse Wrecks) making spacious, dystopian techno; this is a live set, not a DJ set.

zoh amba.note: Tennessee-raised avant-garde jazz saxophonist/flutist mentored by David Murray, known for skronking free-jazz records produced by John Zorn — now signed to Matador and pivoting toward guitar-based folk songwriting. An unusual, interesting opener for an indie-rock bill.

sean rowe.note: Troy, NY singer-songwriter on Anti- Records since 2010 — a booming, weathered baritone the Wall Street Journal compares to Leonard Cohen; alt-folk/Americana built for a small room like this.

swimming bell.note: Alt-folk project with a hazy, mid-'70s Laurel Canyon-leaning sound — thin footprint beyond that, but a plausible, complementary opener for Rowe's stripped-down Americana.

yaego.note: PG County, Maryland-raised producer blending dark, melodic house with cinematic build — a fast-rising TikTok/SoundCloud name ('Fe en Rebelion,' 'HARDX') more than an established club headliner yet.

tavish.note: Venice-native LA warehouse-scene DJ (also a Grammy-winning producer as half of Sid Roams) — industrial disco and acid house; a fixture across the city's underground circuit alongside names like Psychemagik and DJ Garth.

anfisa letyago.note: Naples-scene-turned-global techno DJ/producer (Russian-born, Italy-based) — hypnotic, groove-driven techno/house; Moby tapped her for a 2022 'Go' remix, and she runs her own label N:S:DA.

luke strand.note: Bay Area-raised, LA-based vocalist/multi-instrumentalist (bass, guitar, keys, trumpet) who teaches at Musicians Institute Hollywood — leads this free weekly soul/jazz/R&B hang covering decades of hits with a rotating band.

orlove.note: Touring indie-disco party brand (not a solo DJ) running 250+ 'Midnite City' nights a year across 40+ markets — open-format sets built around Justice/LCD Soundsystem/Daft Punk-style dance-floor indie, not a specific artist booking.

brijean.note: Oakland duo (Brijean Murphy & Doug Stuart) on Ghostly International — Murphy is also the touring percussionist for Poolside and Toro y Moi; their own sound is warm, congas-driven boogie/dream-pop. This is a DJ set, not the live band, so expect disco/house selections in that same breezy register.

giegling.note: The Weimar, Germany label/collective (Traumprinz aka DJ Metatron, Konstantin/Kettenkarussell, Vril, HVL and others) behind some of the most mythologized, hypnotic house and techno of the last decade — genuinely rare to see a Giegling-branded date in LA, though the listing doesn't say which member of the crew is actually playing.

kids in america.note: Touring '80s new-wave/pop tribute band (originally out of Charlotte, NC) covering hits from the decade — not an original act, so genre is pop covers rather than the venue's usual punk/rock.

sub imperium.note: Producer on Occult Rhythms and Askorn Records — labels built around hard, dark, EBM-tinged techno; rougher and more industrial than the refined European techno lane.

frank walker.note: Toronto progressive-house/EDM producer signed to Kygo's Palm Tree Records — melodic, vocal-driven big-room tracks (500M+ streams).

loud luxury.note: Canadian bass-house duo behind the global hit 'Body' — festival-scale, radio-friendly dance-pop.

o b i.note: German hard-techno veteran of 20+ years, runs his own Definition of Hard Techno label — rough, industrial-edged hard techno, not the melodic/peak-time end.

per pleks.note: Dortmund-based schranz/hard-techno producer who topped Beatport's Hard Techno chart in 2023 — a rising name in the harder German scene.

lackey.note: LA synth-punk band (Dante Pinker, Dan Wityak, T Sweeney, Nate Andre) with a handful of releases on Archfiend Records.

2manydjs.note: Belgian brothers David & Stephen Dewaele (aka Soulwax) — legendary 2000s bootleg-mashup mix series 'As Heard On Radio Soulwax'; disco/electro/indie-rock blends on their own Deewee label, still a real festival-level draw two decades on.

deborah de luca.note: Naples-born global techno headliner, dubbed the 'Queen of Naples' — hypnotic, hard-hitting techno on her own Sola_mente Records; a regular DJ Mag Top 100 name and legit festival mainstage act.

anne futagami.note: Possibly the Tokyo techno/house DJ known for playing guitar over her sets, released on Dirtybird alongside Shinichi Osawa — couldn't confirm it's the same artist booked here, so treat with caution.

negativland.note: Bay Area culture-jamming/plunderphonics collective since 1980 — pioneered sample-collage sound art and became infamous for the 1991 'U2' single lawsuit that helped define modern fair-use law; runs their own Seeland Records. A genuinely legendary, rarely-touring cult act.

sue c.note: Bay Area audiovisual artist and Negativland's longtime visual collaborator — live, hands-on analog video/optical processing built to run alongside their sound collage.

irene moon.note: Alter ego of entomologist-turned-performance-artist Katja Seltmann — absurdist sound/performance art blending science, music and theater; a fixture of the West Coast experimental circuit.

dj professor cantaloupe.note: Mitchell Brown — longtime KXLU voice and west-coast noise/experimental scene veteran (Points of Friction, Melon Expander label); pioneered the ambient sample-collage 'Glossolalia' radio show.

green velvet.note: Chicago house legend (Curtis Jones) — Relief/Cajual/Music Man Records, foundational hard-groove Chicago house tracks like 'La La Land' and 'Flash'; one of the genre's actual originators, not a nostalgia booking.

james hype.note: UK tech-house/bass-house DJ-producer — viral 'Ferrari' remix and a PIRATE Copenhagen resident; crossed from underground tech-house into a full mainstage festival draw.

friction.note: UK drum & bass DJ/producer and longtime BBC Radio 1 D&B show host (Shogun Audio) — one of the genre's most established tastemakers.

flava d.note: UK garage/bassline producer (Butterz) — helped define the 2010s UKG/bassline revival; respected underground name that's crossed into bigger festival bookings.

troyboi.note: UK bass/trap producer known for a distinctive chopped-vocal 'trap' sound — a big mainstage draw in the bass-music world, outside the house/techno lane.

walker and royce.note: LA house/tech-house duo — Dirtybird-adjacent, quirky vocal-driven house cuts; a home-turf name on this bill.

sindri.note: Couldn't verify a bio or track record beyond this booking — treat as an unknown local name.

pirupa.note: Italian tech-house producer (Simone Vitullo) — co-founded Repopulate Mars with Jamie Jones; 'Blow Ya Mind' was a genuine 2015 tech-house anthem, plus releases on Defected.

big gigantic.note: Colorado livetronica duo (Dominic Lalli on sax, Jeremy Salken on drums) — blends live instrumentation with electronic/hip-hop/funk production; a real Bonnaroo/Electric Forest-tier festival draw, just outside the house/techno lane.

avalon emerson.note: American techno/house DJ-producer (SF by way of Berlin) — melodic, songwriterly club techno (the Whities-era singles, her '&More' LP); a genuine global-circuit headliner.

sextile.note: LA synth-punk/EBM band (Sacred Bones) that's leaned harder into techno and rave sounds on its newest record — gothy, driving, club-adjacent post-punk; DJ set here rather than live.

ellen allien.note: Berlin techno pioneer and BPitch Control label founder since the '90s — raw, physical, art-damaged techno; about as European-scene as a booking gets.

effy.note: UK (Blackpool/London) DJ-producer doing druggy acid techno and classic-house revivalism — has opened for Helena Hauff, Scuba, Honey Dijon and Peggy Gou.

johnny_health.note: LA underground rave-circuit DJ (Hood Rave/Hellraiser-type parties) — thin bio beyond a busy local DJ résumé.

zastava.note: Detroit post-punk/noise-rock four-piece (Mateja Matic, Arman Bonislawski) — heavy, drone-y, Sonic Youth-indebted; a 'band you should know' per Monster Children, touring the small-room circuit.

fat lady sang.note: LA noise-rock band — jagged riffs and feedback under a surprisingly clean-cut, mod-suit look; a regular around town's DIY/small-venue bills.

gracebones.note: Alias of UK producer James Hancock — 2x gold-selling, Grammy-acknowledged house/garage producer, hosts House of Chic Radio on Select 94.4FM London; has remixed Chaka Khan and Steve 'Silk' Hurley.

dj kita.note: LA DJ, Hood Rave resident known for energetic hip-hop and dance selections — Boiler Room LA and NTS credits.

silhouwet.note: LA DJ specializing in deep house, afro-house, trance, DnB and Jersey club — Boiler Room-featured, part of the Electric Cleaners local-DJ archive series.

lens.note: Brighton drum & bass DJ-producer, Hospital Records mainstay and host of their Rinse FM show — known for dynamic double-drops and eclectic selection; released on Spearhead too.

nighttime.note: LA cosmic-American-folk project led by Eva Louise Goodman — Bandcamp Best New Music for 2023's 'Keeper is the Heart'; the new 'Looking Glass' LP (July 2026) pulled in players from Weyes Blood, Florist and Marina Allen's circles.

strawberry hands.note: Philadelphia songwriter/multi-instrumentalist doing hazy dream-pop/folk — new album covered by Stereogum.

maiya sykes.note: LA vocalist — Voice Season 7 alum, backing-vocal credits for Black Eyed Peas, Macy Gray, Michael Bublé and Rita Ora, featured vocals in 'La La Land'; a genuinely good voice, not just a novelty booking.

marc homer.note: Berlin-based DJ/producer (formerly LA/NYC) and Half & 1/2 label owner — a Gegen and HÖR regular playing techno, club, breaks, baile and ballroom; cites SOPHIE and Aphex Twin as touchstones.

narciss.note: Unverified which artist of this name is booked — there's a Berlin-based melodic-techno/trance producer (Running Back, Lobster Theremin) and a separate Timișoara, Romania techno DJ sharing the alias; treat with low confidence.

cody currie.note: London-born, Berlin-based multi-instrumentalist producer at the front of the jazz-house revival — Toy Tonics debut album praised by BBC 6 Music and Mixmag, plus releases on Classic and Shall Not Fade.

barbara boeing.note: Curitiba-raised, Milan-based Brazilian selector and Toy Tonics artist ('Brasiliana EP') — 15+ years digging, playing disco/house sets rooted in Brazilian rhythm and global crate-digging.

samuel moriero.note: Young Italian hard-techno DJ/producer riding a fast rise on the European underground circuit — raw, industrial-driven, neo-rave sound; a 2025 Marnik collab ('Hard Techno') got real festival pickup. This is his first LA date.

ben ufo.note: London selector and Hessle Audio co-founder — one of the most respected, genre-agnostic DJs of his generation, moving between house, techno, bass and garage without ever landing on one lane; a Rinse FM mainstay and reliable Boiler Room legend. About as close to a proper fabric/London booking as LA gets.

dj gigola.note: Berlin's Paulina Schulz, part of the Live From Earth collective — genre-fluid sets sliding between trance, gabber, acid, breaks and pop, honed at rooms like Berghain; a real European club import, not a tourist booking.

annie lew.note: LA-based rising techno DJ/producer, an Infra and TUNNEL resident — tension-built, hypnotic, rhythm-first sets.

oza.note: Brooklyn-born, LA-based DJ/producer and TUNNEL founder — high-energy sets blending hard house, breaks and techno; the promoter as much as the performer here.

54 ultra.note: New Jersey singer-songwriter John Rodriguez — garage-pop and Latin-soul-inflected indie, recently the featured vocal on ANOTR's disco-house single 'Talk to You'; the one genuinely dance-adjacent surprise on the rock side of this bill.

pressure point.note: Billed on the flyer as a Miami-based selector working dancehall/reggaeton/guaracha; couldn't independently verify a bio beyond the listing text — treat as unconfirmed.

dax j.note: London-born, Berlin-based techno DJ/producer and founder of the Monnom Black label — RA/DJ Mag Top 100 mainstay known for hard, driving techno and legendary 10-hour closing sets at Berghain and Bassiani. The genuine headliner on this bill.

annika wolfe.note: Oxnard-raised DJ/producer/label boss working the electro-techno-EBM frontier — 80s post-punk/new-wave energy filtered through modern techno; has shared stages with DVS1, Truncate and Drumcell (CRSSD, Re/Form Festival).

grace dahl.note: Amsterdam-based techno DJ/producer (Serial Disc Touchers label) with an emotive, high-energy style — Berghain, Awakenings and Boiler Room credits; a rising-name booking, not a filler slot.

max gardner.note: Bay Area techno lifer — founder of Direct to Earth and the Peer label, 15+ years shaping SF's scene with releases on Sonic Groove and Northern Parallels.

samo.note: Recurring co-headliner of this Spiritual Systems monthly alongside Juliet Mendoza — a regular fixture of the night's soulful deep-house-and-garage sound, not a one-off booking.

shay elys.note: Formerly Suga Shay — Philadelphia-raised, decade-plus LA fixture and Beehive resident; an open-format selector working Black dance-music lineage (house, disco, hip-hop, bass) rather than a straight house/techno set.

techno tupac.note: LA-based DJ/producer/vocalist blending hip-hop energy into driving tech-house — released on Dirtybird and Space Yacht, supported by Green Velvet and Chris Lorenzo, with Coachella and Beyond Wonderland sets on his resume. A real name for a free RSVP night, if more festival-leaning than fabric-London.

djrum.note: Felix Manuel, London — jazz-trained producer/DJ (R&S, Ilian Tape) whose all-vinyl, three-turntable sets weave techno, breaks, jungle and ambient into something narrative rather than functional. A genuinely rare, extended (4hr) booking, not a standard tour stop.

mark ernestus.note: Berlin legend — founder of the Hard Wax record shop and one half of Basic Channel/Rhythm & Sound, the duo who invented dub techno. Now runs Ndagga Rhythm Force, fusing that lineage with Senegalese mbalax. A living-history booking that almost never comes through LA; his 3-hour set alone justifies the day.

akanbi.note: Lagos-raised, NY-based DJ (GROOVY GROOVY founder) known for blending tough club rhythms into amapiano and Afro-adjacent sounds before hard turns into techno — the amapiano/bass-music strand on this bill.

the large.note: NYC-scene selector, regularly paired with Akanbi (GROOVY GROOVY, Brooklyn) on amapiano/dancehall/afrobeats-leaning closing sets.

arisa.note: Couldn't verify a bio or track record beyond this booking — treat as an unknown local name.

nic jericho.note: Chicago-native, LA-based house DJ who left a finance career to DJ full time; gigging weekly around Reverb/Voltique-adjacent LA gay nightlife.

masato.note: Couldn't verify a bio or track record beyond this booking — treat as an unknown local name.

hhunter.note: Chicago producer/DJ on the rise in industrial/hard techno — self-taught, has picked up support slots for Sara Landry, Indira Paganotto and Hiroko Yamamura. Harder and more rave than groove; adjacent to the hard-techno lane this taste generally steers around, not the fabric/Innervisions end.

francis mercier.note: Haitian-American Afro house DJ/producer behind the global 'Amazon' hit — founder of Deep Root Records and the Soléy imprint/party brand this event is named for; one of the genre's biggest current global names.

shimza.note: South African Afro-tech pioneer, alum of Black Coffee's Soulistic Music and now running his own Kunye/KSD imprints — a real headline draw on the Afro house/tech circuit.

seamus haji.note: UK house veteran since the '80s, Big Love label boss and former Defected/Strictly Rhythm A&R — remixed everyone from Rihanna to Mariah Carey, held residencies at Pacha Ibiza and Ministry of Sound.

alastair lane.note: French house/indie-dance producer whose 'Roman d'Amour' went viral (a Top 40 most-Shazamed house track globally in 2024) — this show is billed as his US debut.

never dull.note: LA/Tijuana disco-house producer — a multi-year Traxsource top artist with co-signs from Disclosure, Dom Dolla and John Summit.

andy martin.note: Guadalajara-based dub/sci-fi techno producer, co-founder of Mole Audio — released 'Revolution' with Lee 'Scratch' Perry and has played MUTEK and Awakenings; this booking is a rare extended 3-hour set.

ok eg.note: Melbourne live hardware duo (Lauren Squire & Matthew Wilson) working entirely live — releases on Kalahari Oyster Cult and Animalia, known for immersive, evolving techno sets.

sysk.note: LA-based techno/bass-and-breaks DJ, a regular on Canary Sound Werk's TBA-location afterhours bills.

trap girl.note: LA hardcore punk band fronted by trans singer Drew Arriola-Sands, mixing old-school punk with riot-grrrl edge — covered by Remezcla and L.A. TACO as one of LA's real underground acts.

guaparda.note: Estefanía Gallo-Gonzalez (aka Langosta) — LA-based singer, DJ and dublab radio host currently studying to be a music librarian/archivist; house-leaning selections, releases via the dottidot orbit.

beste hira.note: Istanbul-born, Amsterdam-based techno DJ/producer — hypnotic, dark, fast-paced techno; Orphic/DeSchool/Vault Sessions resident, has played Awakenings, ADE and Berghain.

stephen disario.note: LA techno producer, Conundrum Records label boss and Cognition event co-founder — moody, driving techno with support from Amelie Lens and Pan Pot.

takaaki itoh.note: Japanese techno veteran since the early '90s, founder of the WOLS label — dark, hypnotic, driving techno released via Mord and Warm Up; one of Japan's most respected underground techno DJs.

chris liebing.note: German techno veteran since the early-'90s Frankfurt scene, founder of the purist techno label/podcast CLR — a genuine headline-tier name (Awakenings, Time Warp) known for dark, driving, relentless sets; a 5-hour set is a real event, not a normal tour-stop hour.

truncate.note: David Flores — LA producer and co-founder of OBSERVE (with Moe Espinosa/Drumcell); raw, hypnotic, groove-driven techno that's played Berghain, fabric, Concrete and Awakenings. This is his own party's anniversary, not a guest slot.

oktaform.note: Recurring visual artist for OBSERVE's parties (also did visuals for their 2024 Speedy J/Drumcell edition) — no separate DJ/production profile found.

bloody mary.note: French-born, Berlin-based vinyl DJ and producer (real name Marjorie Migliaccio) — hardware-driven house, techno and acid, owns the Dame-Music label; festival credits include Movement Detroit, Sonar and ADE. Genuine European club pedigree.

julia govor.note: NY-based (Russian-born) techno producer/DJ known for hypnotic, meditative techno — JUJUKA label owner, Lot Radio resident, championed by fabric London.

laure croft.note: Dutch-born, Berlin-based DJ who plays strictly vinyl, all-techno sets pulled from the mid-90s to mid-2000s — founder of Sexyrecs, a regular at About Blank, Gegen and RSO. A real all-vinyl European booking, not a marketing label.

electric field.note: SoCal-based analog-house DJ/producer and a recurring name at Level 8's rooftop nights — a home resident more than a touring booking; couldn't verify much beyond the local circuit.

plavka.note: Singer/producer best known as the voice of Jam & Spoon's early-90s trance hits and a former Shamen collaborator — now LA-based and DJing/producing bass house. A genuine dance-music veteran, but her current lane (bass house, vocal-forward) doesn't quite match the tech-house/minimal billing here.

roman flügel.note: Veteran German house/techno producer (Ongaku Musik; "Ganz", "Roman IV") and half of 90s duo Alter Ego — a Live at Robert Johnson/Playhouse-lineage DJ, genuine European club royalty and exactly the fabric/Robert Johnson pedigree this lane is built for.

jane margarette.note: LA DJ playing house/techno around town with residencies at spots like Better Tomorrow and Psstudio — local support, nothing more substantial to verify.

man power.note: UK DJ/producer (Geoff Kirkwood, Newcastle) and boss of the Me Me Me label — genuinely eclectic cosmic disco, dub techno and throwback piano house; a characterful, Balearic-leaning booking rather than a generic tech-house name.

sonns.note: LA underground fixture (Alexandre Mouracade), founder of Making Shapes and the In Between and DISCOS XXX party series, releases on his own Machine Limited label plus Kompakt and ESP Institute — a punk-rooted, synth-into-house selector who's a real name in this scene.

darlene chan.note: Jazz impresario with a five-decade career shaping LA's jazz scene — longtime producer of the Playboy Jazz Festival; being honored here alongside Hancock.

gerald clayton.note: Grammy-winning jazz pianist (son of bassist John Clayton) — a mainstay of the current modern-jazz touring and festival circuit.

billy childs.note: LA-based Grammy-winning pianist/composer, known for orchestral jazz arrangements (including the Laura Nyro tribute album).

izaak opatz.note: Montana-raised, Nashville-then-LA singer-songwriter — wry alt-country/folk-rock songwriting (Mama Bird Recording Co.), 'Extra Medium' LP; formerly of Croy and the Boys.

sie sie benhoff.note: LA singer-songwriter with a powerful, soulful voice and steel-guitar-leaning arrangements (often billed with her band the Sad Sacks) — Sofar Sounds / Echo Park Rising circuit regular.

sherelle.note: London 160bpm force spinning footwork, jungle and dnb — co-founded Hooversound and runs the Black/queer-focused label Beautiful; a fabric/Boiler Room-tier name, not a house purist but a real international draw.

pangaea.note: UK producer, co-founder of Hessle Audio (with Ben UFO, Pearson Sound) — bass-schooled techno that fits the fabric-London end of the lane.

danny daze.note: Miami techno/house producer on Omnidisc and Crosstown Rebels — respected selector on the US underground club circuit.

mia koden.note: South London producer/DJ, half of Sicaria Sound, working the 140bpm dub/garage/steppers space — released on Ilian Tape, RA's 2024 Breakthrough Artist.

klangkuenstler.note: German techno producer (Michael Korb) who built his own Outworld and Zuckerton Records imprints — matured from deep/tech house into hard, acid- and trance-tinged peak-time techno; co-runs the label Tote Sonne with Kobosil.

ashley younniä.note: New Jersey-born, LA-based DJ steeped in Black-American house/gospel/R&B tradition — runs the deep-house residency Feelin' Feelin' and plays regularly around LA's house scene (Stardust, TheyHouseLA).

ravedad.note: LA underground DJ (Maggie Baron), Dublab regular and co-founder of the 90s-throwback afterhours series Serenity Rave.

daedelus.note: LA experimental-beat producer from the Low End Theory/Brainfeeder-adjacent 2000s beat scene — glitchy, genre-blurring sets, a real veteran name for anyone into that lineage.

conducta.note: UK garage producer/DJ who founded Kiwi Rekords and has been central to the 2-step/UKG revival — a real fabric/Boiler Room/Printworks name, not a niche curiosity.

tritonal.note: American trance/progressive-house duo (Chad Cisneros & Dave Reed) on Enhanced/Armada — real festival-circuit history (EDC, Ultra) and a long-running radio show, more big-room anthem than club groove.

will varley.note: UK folk-punk singer-songwriter on Xtra Mile Recordings, part of the Frank Turner touring orbit — wry, road-worn acoustic songs, a real name in that scene.

beans on toast.note: UK folk singer (Jay McAllister) famous for releasing an album every birthday since 2009 — dry, talking-blues folk, another Xtra Mile/Frank Turner-circle regular.

amadeezy.note: Boston-based DJ/producer who co-founded the trap/dirty-south night PVRPLE before moving into house and ghettotech production (International Chrome, Moveltraxx) — a real production pedigree, just not an LA-familiar name.

friendship commanders.note: Nashville doom/sludge/grunge duo (Buick Audra, Jerry Roe) — a 2018 record was cut by Steve Albini, latest LP 'BEAR' is out on Magnetic Eye Records. Real touring pedigree.

doomboyz.note: LA stoner/doom rock band whose 2024 debut 'Evil Riffs From Los Angeles' was tracked at the Foo Fighters' Studio 606 and got Grammy Best Rock Album consideration.

dj godfather.note: Brian Jeffries — Detroit ghettotech founding father, co-founded Twilight 76 and Databass Records in the mid-'90s fusing Detroit techno with Miami bass. This is bass/electro turf, not the house-techno core lane, but he's the real deal in it.

symønne.note: LA-based DJ/producer and founder of Blaque María, an all-woman/queer/BIPOC-centered collective and event brand; started in Boston/Bay Area underground circuits (Burning Man mainstage support) before relocating to LA. Sound leans Chicago house, tech-house, minimal and melodic techno — closer to the taste lane than her ghettotech billmates here.

star amerasu.note: Also records as Ah Mer Ah Su — Black trans multidisciplinary artist/DJ whose project fuses club culture with speculative fiction; Billboard named her 2018 album one of that year's Top 20 LGBTQ+ records. Genre-blurring electronic/art-pop more than a straight house/techno set.

marcel dettmann.note: Berghain resident and one of the defining voices in industrial/minimal techno — co-founded Ostgut Ton; relentless, physical sets, about as proper-European-club-night as it gets.

sol ortega.note: Buenos Aires-born techno producer blurring house and techno with old-school rave energy — Berghain and Boiler Room credits, releases on FJAAK's Crowd label; a genuinely rising international name, not a filler booking.

perel.note: Berlin producer/DJ (Annegret Fiedler) who sings live over her own house-leaning sets — released on Running Back, Kompakt, and Permanent Vacation; warm, vocal-forward, very much the European club sound.

jt donaldson.note: Dallas-raised, Chicago-schooled house veteran since the mid-'90s — debuted on Cajmere's Cajual Records; deep, soulful, wide-ranging sets (house, disco, afrobeat, acid) and a longtime foil for Derrick Carter.

los hermanos flores.note: Founded 1962 in San Vicente, El Salvador — the most prestigious orchestra in Salvadoran music history, credited with breaking cumbia big across Central America with hits like "La Bala" and "Enferma"; still touring after 60+ years.

radio pulgarcito.note: LA-based vinyl DJ project built around Salvadoran cultural identity — spins cumbia, salsa, funk, disco, rock and folklorico from the Salvadoran diaspora catalog, not just cumbia hits.

bobby beethoven fka total freedom.note: Ashland Mines — Fade to Mind co-founder and a genuine architect of the genre-scrambling underground DJ set (GHE20G0TH1K, his own Wildness party); recently rebranded from Total Freedom. Widely cited as one of the most influential living club DJs, even outside the house/techno mainstream.

katie rex.note: Brooklyn techno/industrial DJ and BOUND NYC founder, a Basement resident — dark, hardgroove-leaning sets; brings BOUND to LA and makes her INCOGNITO debut around this booking.

michelle leshem.note: Miami-to-LA DJ with 15+ years behind the decks — known as a disco specialist blending obscure disco, new wave and acid house; runs the Disco + Design platform.

zoraya.note: Detroit-born, LA-based house DJ and dublab host, plays under the Phuture Perfect banner.

dirt vibes.note: LA house DJ known for edgy, groovy sets with deep-house elements — a regular around rooms like Pattern Bar.

beggar.note: LA DJ/producer Jonny Rodriguez, part of the Forward Rhythm collective — deep house shading into neo-soul and rave.

yuka honda.note: Cibo Matto co-founder and a longtime Yoko Ono collaborator/producer — co-writes and directs this piece.

glenn kaino.note: LA conceptual artist known for politically engaged multimedia work — co-directs alongside Honda.

nels cline.note: Wilco's guitarist and, outside that band, a serious free-jazz/experimental improviser — part of the backing ensemble here.

manuka honey.note: US-born, London-based DJ (Marissa Malik) fusing Latin club sounds — cumbia, dembow, reggaeton — into UK club production; BBC Radio 1 and Rinse FM resident, runs the SUZIO party series.

rose kourts.note: Brooklyn DJ/radio host and Sweet Kicks founder — swung acid house and freakified techno; has played direct support for Moodymann, Mr. G, and Kevin Saunderson at rooms like Nowadays and Basement.

1morning.note: LA producer specializing in all-vinyl, old-school swung techno and hardgroove (Fixed Rhythms, Mala Adh) in the lineage of Robert Armani and DJ Rush — played Tresor and Draaimolen this year.

tahl us.note: LA DJ and WAK Music co-founder, recently back from six years in Berlin — ranges house/techno/breaks/electro; this is his own crew's night.

olivia powers.note: LA DJ who co-runs the Wormhole party and sings in the band Sivil^3.

zenker brothers.note: Dario and Marco Zenker, the Munich brothers behind Ilian Tape — dubby, hypnotic techno/electro that's been the label's signature since 2007; this is an extended (open-to-close-style) set, not a quick guest slot.

oj us.note: LA producer/DJ leaning leftfield, nostalgic rave sounds with an underground edge.

riria.note: Tokyo-born, London-based selector blending UK garage, amapiano, Jersey club and dub — her 2024 Boiler Room set hit ~5M views, Mixmag named her a 2025 Breakthrough DJ, and she's now a Rinse FM resident.

trekkie trax crew.note: Tokyo collective (andrew, Carpainter, futatsuki, Seimei) behind the genre-agnostic Trekkie Trax label — house, techno, footwork and juke, with support from Ben UFO and Gilles Peterson.

angel cannon.note: Vancouver-based hard-techno/hardstyle producer-vocalist ('The Green Machine') — releases on Scantraxx and Barong Family, has played EDC Las Vegas; real cred within that scene.

onur özer.note: Istanbul-born, Ibiza/Cocoon-circuit techno DJ — releases on Cocoon Recordings and Vakant since the mid-2000s, longtime Amnesia/DC10 name; deep, hypnotic, properly European in feel.

mayell.note: Slovenian house/deep-house DJ (Luckison crew) who's shared stages with Onur Özer, Craig Richards and Zip — the kind of booking that signals a curated, not generic, lineup.

luciid.note: Irish producer (Luke Pollock) and founder of the AGONY imprint — a genuine Beatport-charting schranz/hard-techno name; sets typically build from groove into 145-150bpm techno before tipping into schranz.

callush.note: Berlin-based producer (Carolina Z.) running her own label Riot Tapes — dark industrial techno shot through with EBM and trance, a real fixture on the European hard-techno circuit (DGTL, Mixmag Germany features).

tommy oeffling.note: Milwaukee-bred indie/slacker-rock songwriter getting real press buzz right now — touring the West Coast with his full band, the B-Team.

dossey.note: Austin-based "glitter grunge" pop/indie-pop artist — melodic, hooky songwriting (Animal EP), a real touring act rather than an unknown local opener.

jesse detor.note: Boston indie-pop songwriter with a real Spotify following (~45K monthly listeners) — 90s-rock-tinged, confessional pop in the Veruca Salt/Phoebe Bridgers vein.

carmela.note: LA-based indie-rock songwriter (debut album New Stranger) with a devoted following built off years of livestreamed performances — press-covered (Grimy Goods) and has toured internationally.

yellow shoots.note: Brooklyn multi-instrumentalist (Gregory Matthews) making genre-bending psych/R&B — warm, off-kilter soul rather than a straight rock bill.

kevin roosevelt.note: LA-born R&B artist (son of Keb' Mo') who's charted on the R&B charts and collaborated with Jhené Aiko and Rapsody — a real name playing a small room.

the killing floors.note: LA five-piece rock 'n' roll band built on 60s garage and punk influences — Music Connection named them one of the Top 100 Live Performers.

the street walkin cheetahs.note: Veteran LA punk/hard-rock band (named for the Stooges' "Search and Destroy"), fronted by Frank Meyer, with members who've shared stages with Radio Birdman's Deniz Tek, MC5's Wayne Kramer, and the New York Dolls' Sylvain Sylvain — real proto-punk lineage, not a tribute act.

lukas and frank.note: German-Austrian duo who paired up in late 2024 — Lukas plays live saxophone, Frank live cello, layered over Afro/melodic/organic house selections; a fast-growing 'Sax & Cello' mix series has built them real momentum in under two years.

subb an.note: UK DJ/producer and Crosstown Rebels/Damian Lazarus protégé — DJ Mag's Best Breakthrough DJ in 2011, runs his own One Records imprint; warm, rolling deep/tech-house in the Rebel Rave lineage.

calvin love.note: Edmonton songwriter who emerged from the same Canadian scene as Mac DeMarco and Alex Calder — dark, synth-driven bedroom pop/post-punk rather than a straight rock band, despite how this bill reads on paper.

john moods.note: Solo project of Jonathan J. (co-founder of Berlin band Fenster) — shimmering, psychedelic soft-pop, largely written and produced on an iPhone; released via the Mansions and Millions label.

kyle watson.note: Johannesburg-raised, now-touring tech-house producer — co-owner of the bass-leaning Box of Cats label, with festival slots at Ultra, EDC and Lollapalooza. Jacking, peak-time tech-house rather than a deep/vinyl selector.

jack marlow.note: Liverpool-bred UK garage prodigy in his early twenties, drawing on Sammy Virji and Kettama's house-meets-garage sound — already played Boomtown, Night Tales and Pamela in Paris; one of the names actually pushing current UK garage forward.

gee lee.note: House DJ/producer blending live instrumentation into Boiler-Room-style sets, touring basement clubs in Berlin and Paris through festivals in Australia and Mexico.

zig zags.note: LA punk-metal power trio (Black Sabbath/Black Flag/Motörhead energy) on In The Red Records — Ty Segall produced their debut, and they've backed Iggy Pop and toured with Osees, Fuzz and Pentagram. Real scene pedigree, not a local opener.

golden grease.note: LA post-punk/garage/krautrock unit whose debut LP 'Zero Time' came out on Permanent Records itself — rips through hardcore and krautrock influences in barely 22 minutes.

aaron paar.note: LA scene veteran since the early '90s (fka DJ Destroyer) — Worldship Music/Umoja Hi-Fi affiliate with a long-running Dublab radio show, deep across soul, disco and vintage house.

darone sassounian.note: LA DJ/producer and Rocky Hill label boss — monthly Club Tee Gee residency since 2019, Dublab radio residency, releases on Habibi Funk and Terrestrial Funk; disco, soul, jazz and vintage-house digging (not the h.wood nightlife exec of the same name).

noah selene.note: LA-based DJ and fashion photographer active on the queer-underground electronic circuit.

emanate.note: SF-based house/techno duo (Emily Fox & Nathan Vain) who run their own label, Mioli Music, built around rooftop series and open-to-close sets that move through deep house, tech-house and techno.

petit biscuit.note: French producer Mehdi Benjelloun — broke out with the 2015 downtempo hit 'Sunset Lover'; lush, melodic electronica closer to ODESZA/Bonobo territory than house or techno, with genuine festival-headliner credits (Coachella, Lollapalooza).

forester.note: Indie-electronic producer and frequent Petit Biscuit collaborator (their joint single 'Close Your Eyes') — same atmospheric, melodic-minimalist lane.

sam divine.note: British DJ/producer known as the 'Queen of Defected' — signed to Defected Records in 2009, has hosted their weekly radio show and anchored their Ibiza residencies for over a decade; polished, vocal-driven house.

tawanda.note: LA-based jazz vocalist (Tawanda Suessbrich-Joaquim) — won the 2020 Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition; her 2022 debut album 'Smile' came out on Resonance Records.

wax motif.note: Sydney-born, LA-based producer (Danny Chien) and a defining voice in G-house/bass house — releases on Confession, Mad Decent, Fool's Gold; big, filthy low-end over subtlety.

dance spirit.note: LA duo (Christopher Mohn & Reagan Denius) on Get Physical, Crosstown Rebels and Bedrock — heavy-low-end, futuristic minimal/progressive house, deep in the Desert Hearts family.

robotek reagan.note: Reagan Denius's solo alias — literally one half of Dance Spirit, so this bill is really the duo playing twice under two names.

jackson englund.note: LA DJ/producer and Gari Safari co-founder who folds neo-soul, funk and jazz into house; released on Desert Hearts.

seven lions.note: Jeff Montalvo — melodic dubstep/bass pioneer and Ophelia Records founder; the genre-defining name pulling this bill outside the house/techno lane.

tokimonsta.note: LA producer (Jennifer Lee) — Grammy-nominated future-beat/bass artist and one of the first women to headline a Coachella mainstage set; genre-blending rather than straight house/techno.

tchami.note: French DJ/producer who coined 'future house' and runs the Confession label/party brand — the more house-leaning name on an otherwise bass-heavy bill.

oliver heldens.note: Dutch producer — broke out with 2014's 'Gecko,' a future-house pioneer alongside Tchami; also runs a deeper techno alias, HI-LO.

gordo.note: Formerly Carnage — the trap/EDM producer rebranded into house a few years back and now runs with the Solid Grooves crowd; a genuine lane-shift, not just a rename.

flosstradamus.note: Chicago duo (Curt Cameruci, Josh Young) — one of the acts that built festival trap in the early 2010s, still a heavy bass-stage draw.

mija.note: LA bass/house DJ-producer in the Brownies & Lemonade orbit — eclectic, genre-hopping sets that land more bass-forward than house.

r3hab.note: Dutch big-room/progressive house DJ-producer (Cyb3rpvnk) — festival-mainstage staple for over a decade.

rrose.note: US techno producer/performer known for hypnotic, physically intense techno (Eaux, Stroboscopic Artefacts orbit) — one of the more respected voices in abstract, mind-bending techno right now.

wata igarashi.note: Tokyo-based producer whose cerebral, psychedelic, hypnotic techno (Midgar Records) has made him a genuinely in-demand international touring name.

marrøn.note: Jessey Voorn — Dutch/Surinamese DJ known for rhythmic, tribal-inflected techno pulling on African percussion; co-founder/resident of Amsterdam's EERSTE COMMUNIE.

rene wise.note: Brighton-born, Portugal-based DJ/producer (Mote-Evolver, his own Moving Pressure label) — hypnotic, groovy, rolling 90s-leaning techno; backed by Rødhad, Blawan and DVS1.

sarah wreath.note: Berlin-based sound artist and live techno producer — deep, psychedelic, hypnotic sets; debut LP 'Integration' on The Bunker New York, plus a Sandwell District collaboration.

jia.note: Founder of 6AM Group and co-founder of LA's RE/FORM Festival — a connector/promoter as much as a DJ, with residencies at Factory 93 and Beyond Wonderland.

nekter.note: LA-based techno DJ, 2021 REFORM DJ Contest winner (6AM Group/Synthetik Minds) — resident at WORK LA, playing hypnotic, texture-heavy techno sets.

pablo bozzi.note: Berlin-based producer working what he calls 'Italo Body Music' — Italo disco slammed into EBM, synthwave and industrial. Own label Second Sight, a Berghain/Panorama Bar regular, viral 2023 Boiler Room set at Khidi.

neofx.note: Paris/Berlin-based hard-techno, acid and neorave producer — fast, hard-hitting 150-165bpm tracks, 5M+ plays and 50K+ monthly listeners. A different, faster lane than the house/techno spine.

rodriguez jr.note: French producer Olivier Mateu (mentored by Laurent Garnier, came up via F-Communications) — 20+ years into a warm, cinematic strain of melodic house/techno, records on Mobilee, Anjunadeep and Systematic.

kenny dope.note: One half of the legendary Masters at Work (with Louie Vega) — 30+ years deep into foundational NYC house; the single most significant name on this bill.

kitty amor.note: London-based Afro house DJ, Get Physical/Mahaba Music — founded Motherland, an Afro house platform/collective; regular at Hi Ibiza and Grow London.

canary yellow.note: LA-based DJ/producer (Denver-raised), a fixture of the local club scene — house and club-edit tracks out on Traxsource.

faster horses.note: UK (Manchester) DJ Joe Germains, describes his sound as trance/techno/psychedelia — plays for the Teletech and Interplanetary Criminal party circuits; releases on Euromantic and RAW.

azyr shankz starrza tdj natte visstick d.note: The extended Teletech crew Faster Horses reps (the Manchester-born hard/fast-techno collective now touring globally) filling out the bill — couldn't verify individual bios beyond that co-billing, so treat this stretch as a wildcard.

matt egbert.note: LA deep-house producer and Front Left Recordings/Productions founder (events in LA, San Diego, NYC, Miami) — multiple Beatport #1 deep-house releases; galactic synths, twisted vocals, groove-forward.

sumkind.note: LA-based electronic artist blending live instrumentation (keys, guitar, vocals) over heavy bass and atmospheric production — more hybrid live-set energy than a straight DJ set; thin public footprint beyond local bookings, so take as lightly verified.

evade robots.note: LA-based producer/DJ (South Texas-raised, bass-player background) rooted in the Low End Theory beat scene — atmospheric, downtempo-leaning electronic; released the 'Voids' LP on Low Recordings, the label behind this night. The one verifiable name on the bill.

kozlov.note: French producer (Florian Kozlowski) working hard techno/schranz/industrial — tracks like 'Tchernobyl' have real circulation in that circuit. A genuine touring name in the hard-techno lane, not a local fill-in.

rilo kiley.note: Jenny Lewis's 2000s LA indie-rock band — jangly, literate power-pop out of the Silver Lake scene; reunited in 2024 after a 15-year hiatus, so a live set is still a real occasion.

beachwood sparks.note: LA cosmic-country/psych band (Sub Pop, later Alive Naturalsound) — Gram Parsons/Byrds-descended twang that ran alongside Rilo Kiley in the early-2000s Silver Lake scene.

sohmi.note: Korean-American, LA-based DJ/producer/vocalist blending minimal house and techno with her own R&B-inflected singing — releases on Astralwerks and Nothing Else Matters, a regular on the Insomniac festival circuit.

familiar faces.note: A multi-city (LA, NYC, Portland, Phoenix, Vegas...) open-format day-party brand built around crowd energy and photos rather than a curated DJ bill — draws up to ~2,000 guests per stop.

shefa.note: Couldn't verify a substantive bio — no confirmed public profile as a touring DJ; treat as unproven/local until more turns up.
