armand van helden.note: Grammy-winning house/garage veteran since the '90s ('You Don't Know Me,' half of Duck Sauce) — a genuinely legacy name for an afternoon park party.

james poole.note: Rising North-of-England house DJ/producer — releases on Hot Creations, Elrow and Experts Only, directly in the fabric/Hot Creations European house orbit.

athena.note: Couldn't verify a confident bio for this booking — flagging as unknown rather than guessing.

nelzon.note: A recurring Sunday Sessions resident (recorded sets from past editions are online) — couldn't pin down a fuller bio beyond that, so treat as an unknown quantity.

roman a.note: Couldn't verify a confident bio for this name — flagging rather than guessing.

olivia dean.note: British neo-soul/pop singer-songwriter (Mercury-nominated album 'Messy') — warm, jazz-inflected pop, leans more soul-show than dance.

khruangbin.note: Houston trio — hypnotic, largely wordless psych-soul/funk built on Thai-funk-inspired guitar; now a genuine amphitheater-level draw.

durand jones and the indications.note: Indiana retro-soul band (Dead Oceans) — horn-driven, deeply '60s/'70s soul-revival sound.

hiatus kaiyote.note: Melbourne 'future soul' band led by Nai Palm — dense, virtuosic jazz-funk that's drawn Grammy nods and real respect from the Thundercat/D'Angelo circle.

erez.note: NY/LA-based producer-vocalist — sultry, emotionally-charged house released via Crosstown Rebels, DFTD (Defected) and Get Physical.

bawab.note: Couldn't verify a confident bio for this DJ — flagging as unknown rather than guessing.

mallrat.note: Grace Shaw — Brisbane dream-pop/indie artist known for wistful, synth-laced tracks like 'Charlie' and 'Rockstar'; more atmospheric bedroom-pop than club music.

holy sun opera house.note: LA duo of opera singer/drummer Krissy Barker and composer dl Salo (A Story of Rats, Saint Genet) — symphonic synths, operatic vocals and heavy drums, self-titled debut just out on Hologram Opera.

carolyn pennypacker riggs.note: LA composer and multimedia artist working across sound, sculpture and ritual-performance; leads the resistance-chorus project Community Chorus and is half of the pop duo Bouquet.

anenon.note: Brian Allen Simon — LA ambient/jazz producer and Non Projects label founder who folds his own saxophone into dreamy, abstract electronic-jazz soundscapes (Friends of Friends' 'Petrol'). A live set, not a DJ set.

parallelle.note: Amsterdam-based Dutch brothers (Thomas & Julien de Bie) — groovy, instrumental-heavy live/DJ hybrid sets blending jazz and classical roots with electronic waves; play fabric London, Pacha Ibiza and their own Klassified imprint.

tim green.note: UK producer (DJ Mag's Best Breakthrough Producer, 2010) — lush, warm deep house/minimal-techno crossover; fabric and Watergate Berlin regular, released on Dirtybird and Cocoon.

birds of mind.note: Paris duo running Mindgame Records — organic house built for the All Day I Dream sound, a label regular alongside Bedouin.

verraco.note: Medellín producer, TraTraTrax/Insurgentes co-founder — percussive, bass-heavy leftfield club music blending Latin rhythm with techno and IDM; XL Recordings signee, Pitchfork Best New Music EP in 2024. A real underground-scene name, not a filler booking.

darwin.note: Canadian-born, Berlin-based DJ and SPE:C label founder — runs REEF, Berlin's go-to night for soundsystem-leaning bass music (techno, dubstep, breaks, DnB); genuinely respected curator, not a genre tourist.

carré.note: LA-to-London producer and Fast At Work co-founder — bass music and percussive leftfield techno, debuted on Darwin's SPE:C label and more recently on the storied dubstep label Tempa.

samwise.note: LA underground techno/breaks DJ tied to the Fast At Work circuit — limited public track record beyond local bookings.

pawsa.note: London tech-house DJ, co-founder of Solid Grooves Records (with Michael Bibi) — stripped-back, groove-led tech-house built for a proper dancefloor, plus his own PAWZ imprint for the odder cuts.

bart skils.note: Dutch techno producer, Second State co-founder (with Pig&Dan) — driving, festival-scale Drumcode-adjacent techno; a 4-hour open-to-close set is a real commitment from a real name.

dvs1.note: Minneapolis techno DJ, Hospital Productions co-founder and Mistress imprint boss — one of the most respected working techno DJs globally, closely tied to the Berghain axis. A 4-hour set is a real event, not a stop-through.

mary yuzovskaya.note: Berlin-based (Moscow-born) techno DJ and Monday Off label head — psychedelic, hypnotic techno; a Berghain/Tresor regular in her own right.

maesic.note: London-born, France-raised DJ (Emeric Boxall) — tech-house/Afro house/melodic-techno crossover; 2025 breakout viral hit with Marshall Jefferson, signed to WME. More big-room crossover than underground.

rebūke.note: Irish producer (Reuben Keeney), Drumcode mainstay since 2019 — driving techno with a house/'90s-rave undertow; his 'Along Came Polly' topped Beatport's tech-house chart for two months.

biscits.note: UK tech-house producer on Hot Since 82's Knee Deep In Sound and Sola Records — bouncy, festival-friendly tech-house rather than deep/groove-leaning.

nicky romero.note: Dutch DJ/producer, Protocol Recordings founder — global big-room/progressive-house festival name ('Toulouse'); more mainstream EDM than the house/techno lane, but a genuine headliner-tier act in a nightclub room.

morenxxx.note: Chicago underground DJ/producer (Jesús Hilario Reyes) — hypnotic, fast-moving sets spanning techno, house and performance-art-adjacent sound work; a genuinely left-of-center booking for a TBA warehouse night.

loukeman.note: Toronto producer/multi-instrumentalist (Luke Fenton) — lo-fi, pitch-shifted outsider house blurring house, R&B and indietronica; has collaborated with A$AP Rocky, Aminé, PinkPantheress and MIKE. A crate-digger pick, not a big-room name.

dyltwosix.note: LA experimental rap/producer and regular collaborator with Loukeman's crew (BRXZN WXRLD nights) — local scene support rather than a solo draw.

magdalena bay.note: LA synth-pop duo (Mica Tenenbaum & Matthew Lewin) — lush, maximalist, internet-fluent synth-pop (Mercurial World, Imaginal Disk); more pop than club but electronic-production-obsessed.

jane remover.note: Hyperpop/digicore pioneer turned shoegaze — restless genre-hopper (Frailty, Census Designated, Revengeseekerz); a cult name in the extremely-online electronic underground.

bag raiders.note: Australian electro-pop/nu-disco duo (Jack Glass & Chris Stracey) on Modular Records — best known for 'Shooting Stars,' the 2009 single that went viral years later as the falling-meme song; polished, hook-heavy electro-house from the late-2000s Modular/Cut Copy wave.

css.note: Brazilian dance-punk/electroclash band (Lovefoxxx on vocals) — 'Music Is My Hot Hot Sex' was a mid-2000s indie-sleaze anthem; toured with Bloc Party and M.I.A. in that era.

geese.note: Brooklyn art-rock band, jittery post-punk energy with a big breakout run recently.

hugel.note: French house/tech-house producer, known for the Latin-tinged 'Bella Ciao' remix and big festival sets.

ben klock.note: Berghain resident and Ostgut Ton regular, the hypnotic, driving end of Berlin techno.

blawan.note: UK producer whose raw, bass-heavy techno sits closer to the Hessle Audio/Ternesc side of things.

gerd janson.note: Running Back boss, a Frankfurt digger who moves between disco, house and weirder club music.

east end dubs.note: UK techno and tech-house producer with a groove-first, rolling sound.

osunlade.note: Founder of Yoruba Records, a spiritual, soulful deep-house producer and DJ known for his Ibiza and Detroit connections.

horse meat disco.note: London disco collective whose Vauxhall residency grew out of a gay Sunday night; a long-running name in the Balearic-disco and nu-disco world.

helena hauff.note: Hamburg techno and electro DJ, hard and acid-leaning, Ninja Tune and Tresor orbit.

haai.note: London DJ and producer, psychedelic techno on Targ and Mute.

satoshi tomiie.note: Japanese-born house veteran who worked with Frankie Knuckles (Tears); here billed live.

james zabiela.note: UK progressive/tech DJ known for hands-on, technical multi-deck sets.

channel tres.note: Compton producer/vocalist blending deep house, hip-hop and funk; a live act as much as a DJ.

camelphat.note: Liverpool duo (Dave Whelan and Mike Di Scala) behind Cola; tech-leaning melodic house at festival scale.

mayan warrior.note: Burning Man art car known for its big sound system; this is its Halloween full-car date.

deorro.note: LA-raised big-room house producer, now mixing in Latin club and regional Mexican crossovers.

will sparks.note: Australian producer who helped popularize Melbourne bounce, a pounding electro-house offshoot.

dimitri vegas.note: Belgian big-room DJ, half of Dimitri Vegas & Like Mike (Tomorrowland mainstage regulars).

innellea.note: German melodic-techno producer with a dark, cinematic sound, released on Afterlife; a regular on bigger room circuits.

rafael cerato.note: Melodic techno/house DJ-producer; support billing here.

dekmantel soundsystem.note: Touring format of Amsterdam's Dekmantel label/festival, a taste-maker house, techno and electro-leaning selection.

massano.note: Progressive/melodic house and techno producer; this is billed as a 360-degree set, an in-the-round format.

actress.note: Darren Cunningham, UK, runs Werkdiscs - smudged, off-kilter techno and house that sits closer to art-music than peak-time.

sander kleinenberg.note: Dutch progressive/tech-house DJ and Little Mountain Recordings founder; a 2000s big-room-meets-underground name who still tours.

bambi.note: French act on the bill; I could not verify specifics, so no further annotation.
